content:
maria.chen: heads-up: we need a short public message and status-page text for the ongoing p99 latency incident affecting /v1/generate. drafting below, please review quickly — we want consistency across tweet, status page, and customer email. on-call handoff: @devon is taking over at 11:30PT. incident-bot: paging history attached.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T10:30Z - High p99 latency - service degraded - paging sent to oncall

devon: I’m on it. thanks @maria. quick note — customer impact is generation requests for larger contexts (>=4k) hitting 2-3x latency. smaller requests unaffected. working with runtime team on a temporary kernel fallback.

aj: for external comms we should avoid technical detail in the tweet. high-level, acknowledge, ETA for update, and link to status. marketing/legal to sign off before post.

sam_marketing: draft tweet suggestion: "We’re investigating increased latency for some text-generation requests. Our team is working on mitigation — we’ll update here and on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai"  (120 chars) :thinking_face:

priya_ops: status page draft (short notice block) — please confirm wording follows the internal incident severity guidance:

```
Summary: Customers may experience elevated latency for text generation endpoints (not affecting embeddings).
Status: Identified
Impacted: A subset of generate requests with large contexts
Start time: 2026-03-15 10:27 UTC
Workaround: Retry smaller context or lower token limit; temporary fallback being rolled out
Next update: 30 minutes
```

erin_security: legal/Trust note — avoid promising exact ETA. ok to say "working on mitigation" and "next update". avoid calling it an outage if we can call it degraded.

maria.chen: good call, @erin_security. change "ETA" -> "next update" in all drafts. sam, can you shorten tweet to drop the status URL (we'll post status link as first reply from the account)? we prefer the tweet to be concise.

sam_marketing: updated tweet: "We’re investigating increased latency for some text-generation requests. We’re working on mitigation and will post updates." (will add first-reply with status link) :white_check_mark:

devon: confirm status page block ok with ops wording above. technical readers: the mitigation will be a fallback kernel that reduces beam-parallelism, likely giving immediate latency improvement but slightly higher token cost. not for public comms.

aj: customer email draft for affected customers (short):

```
Subject: Notice: Temporary elevated latency for text-generation requests

Hi —
We’re reaching out to let you know that some text-generation requests may experience increased latency due to a runtime performance regression. Our engineering team has identified the cause and is rolling a mitigation. We’ll send another update within 30 minutes and a full post-incident summary when resolved.

If you observe production impact that blocks your app, please reply to this email or contact your account team.

Thanks,
The Redwood Inference Team
```

priya_ops: ops checklist for posting: 1) get legal/trust ack (:erin_security) 2) on-call confirms initial mitigation is deployed 3) status page updated 4) tweet queued and authorizes posting time 5) add customer-notify list. I’ll coordinate the status page update and release window.

erin_security: ack on legal side. wording looks fine. do not include internal escalation details.

devon: mitigation rollout starting 10:58 UTC now (canary), will promote by 11:10 if metrics look good. I’ll post metrics snippet in this thread.

incident-bot: deploy started by devon at 1769123900 — canary layer enabled

maria.chen: PR approval flow for social: sam will create the post in social queue, tag @aj for final sign-off, @erin_security for legal sign-off, then publish. timeline goal is 11:15PT.

sam_marketing: creating the queued post now with tweet body above. tagging @aj and @erin_security. also adding suggested first-reply: "Status and progress: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1769123456"

aj: quick editorial tweak: change "We’re investigating" -> "We’re aware of" — stronger signal we have visibility. new tweet: "We’re aware of increased latency for some text-generation requests. We’re working on mitigation and will post updates."

maria.chen: good. legal still ok? @erin_security

erin_security: still good. approved. :white_check_mark:

devon: canary metrics look promising — p99 down ~40% in canary region. promoting to 50% now. will report back in 5m.

maria.chen: once promoted and stable for 2 windows, ops will flip status to "Monitoring" and publish customer email. we should ensure the status page and tweet messaging say the same thing. small copy check: status page uses "elevated latency"; tweet says "increased latency" — fine, minor but consistent enough. prefer to keep identical phrasing if possible.

sam_marketing: changed tweet to match status page: "We’re aware of elevated latency for some text-generation requests. We’re working on mitigation and will post updates." queued and awaiting final send.

priya_ops: promoted to 50% at 1769124050, observed p99 improvement in Canary, promoting to full in 10 minutes if no regression.

devon: full rollout started at 1769124150. no regressions seen in initial windows.

maria.chen: final checks before external publish: legal ok (yes), on-call confirms mitigation deployed (yes), status page updated (priay_ops done), marketing queued tweet (sam queued). I’ll publish the tweet once priya says "Monitoring" on status page.

priya_ops: status page updated to "Monitoring" at 1769124200. next update scheduled in 1 hour. customer email queued to send to customers in affected cohort.

sam_marketing: publishing tweet now. posted at 1769124210. link to status page in first-reply.

maria.chen: thank you everyone. follow-ups: post-incident summary to include root cause, mitigation timeline, and any customer-facing compensations (if applicable). assigning postmortem to @devon and @priya_ops.

devon: will own the RCA draft. thanks.

maria.chen: closing thread for external comms alignment — keep this open for any follow-up notes. :handshake:
